This is the roster's first rotorcraft, so the contrast it draws is not against the Eclipse or
the Stampede on their own terms — it does not corner, it does not brake, and it has no gears.
What it has is the third axis. It is a seventh of the Stampede's mass, it cannot take a hit,
and it can be anywhere on the map in a straight line.
The reference machine is an Airbus H125 (AS350 B3 Ecureuil), which the supplied art is close
to in every measurement that matters: a three-blade main rotor, a shrouded tail rotor, skid
gear and a ten-metre airframe. The model's disc is 9.45 m against the H125's 10.69 m, so the
rotor figures below are the real machine's scaled to the disc the art actually has, rather
than the published ones copied across.
The mass is an operating weight, not the H125's 2,250 kg maximum: empty (1,174 kg) plus fuel,
crew and a weapon fit. At MTOW a helicopter has by definition no thrust margin left, and the
first build flew at 2,250 kg against a 22.4 kN disc — a hover trim of 0.98, which the model
